status: PROPOSAL — staged. Erik ratified all three calls: demotion OK · apexes cycle (legends are MADE by lasting) · re-space the weights and add a tier above legendary.

eriksCalls.1_demotion: YES — authored figures may be re-tiered.
eriksCalls.2_apexes: NO, apexes should NOT be permanently legendary. Erik: 'tradition apexes can and should have legendary, epics, and heroes that come and go... THE ONES THAT STAY THE LONGEST ARE THE TRUE LEGENDS.' ⚠️ THIS IS THE BIGGEST REFRAME IN THE WHOLE SYSTEM: tier stops being an authored label and becomes an EARNED POSITION. A legend is not someone I wrote as great — it is someone the world failed to kill.
eriksCalls.3_ladder: YES — re-space, and add a rung ABOVE legendary because legendaries can keep growing. Quantities INVERTED into a real pyramid.

theLadder.note: Six rungs. Erik: 'a lot of heroes, many epics, a group of legends, only a handful of mythicals.'
spacingRationale: OLD: legendary 50 / epic 45 — a gap of FIVE, so the top two rungs were mechanically the same and CCode's tier-gap mechanic had nothing to read. That was the deeper bug beneath the population problem.

NEW gaps: 22 / 16 / 12 / 12 / 7 — every step is a real step, and the steps GROW toward the top, so distance from the summit costs more than distance from the floor. A mythic outclasses a legend by more than a legend outclasses an epic.

`heroic` REPLACES `regional` as rung 2. Erik's word, and CCode's own code comments already assumed it existed: worldtick.js:875 reads 'a legend holds a couple of fronts; an epic one; A HEROIC FIGURE HALF OF ONE.' The budget tiering was written for a rung the ladder did not have.
⚠️ `regional` MUST STAY MAPPED, not deleted. encounterFrame.js:109 branches on `tier === 'regional'`. Alias regional→heroic at read time; deleting the string breaks live encounter framing.
theLadder.mythicIsSpecial: Erik: 'some legendaries are beyond 50 — they can get more powerful, right?' YES, and mythic is the rung for it. But mythic should be REACHED, not authored: it is what a legendary becomes after surviving long enough and winning enough. A handful at most, and the world should be able to have ZERO.

thePyramid.note: Inverted from today. Current: 60 legendary / 5 epic / 1 regional / 0 below.
thePyramid.howTheRE-TIERINGDERIVES: SCOPE OF WANT, measured from the authored text — 18 world-remaking · 25 craft/regional · 19 personal. That maps almost exactly onto legendary/epic/heroic, so the pyramid was already written and only the tier field was wrong. The bottom two rungs CANNOT be re-tiered into — nothing exists there — so notable and riffraff are a MINTING job, which is why CCode is right that minting is now urgent from both ends.
whatThisFixes: ganging-up becomes possible (there is finally someone to gang up WITH)
the tier-gap mechanic gets gaps to read (2-tier reaches become common instead of nonexistent)
attrition stops being flat — a heroic figure dying to a legend is the expected case, not a sample of one
and promotion has somewhere to come FROM

promotionByDuration.note: ⚠️ ERIK'S REFRAME, MADE MECHANICAL — 'the ones that stay the longest are the true legends.'
promotionByDuration.principle: TIER IS EARNED BY SURVIVING, not assigned by the author. A figure who holds their position across enough world-time and enough contests rises a rung.

proposedRule.heroic→epic: survive ~2 world-years while holding at least one arc care
proposedRule.epic→legendary: survive ~4 world-years AND win contests on an arc they drive or defend
proposedRule.legendary→mythic: survive ~8 world-years as legendary AND remain unbeaten in epic clashes
proposedRule.demotion: ⚠️ A WOUNDED FIGURE WHO ABANDONS EVERY FRONT SHOULD FALL A RUNG. Erik's framing implies it: if lasting is what makes a legend, then failing to last should cost the title.

promotionByDuration.whyThisIsTheGoodVersion: It makes the world's history legible. A player returning after 6 world-years can be told WHO ROSE — and the answer will differ per world, because the arcs already diverge. It also gives the death rate meaning: every legend who dies opens a seat somebody climbs into.
promotionByDuration.andItAnswERSTheMintingQuestion: Minted figures enter at riffraff/notable and CLIMB. The population pyramid maintains itself instead of needing to be re-authored.

openForErik: Is `mythic` the right word? Alternatives: `mythal`, `apex`, `the named`. Erik used 'mythicals'.

Promotion cadence: my 2/4/8 world-year thresholds are a first guess and want CCode's sim to check that they produce a handful of legends rather than sixty again in twenty years.
